newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 92 -1 on last week
Shank (90 CL) 84 +1
Trimmings (85 CL) 76 +1
Chucks (85 CL) 77 n/c
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 148 +6 on last week
Chilled grassfed loin:striploin 245 +5
cube roll 300 +5
tender loin 447 +4

Frozen Thick flank 103 n/c
Frozen Fore/hind blended 83 +3

AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle markets moved higher again this week while lamb markets were also stronger.
Rain, low supplies and slightly firmer export markets contributed to the cattle market rise. Rain in Queensland reduced yardings and boosted restocker competition.

The Queensland cattle market index ended the week four points higher on 104.3 points. Bullocks at Toowoomba this week sold on average for A$2.00 a kg, up a full 60 cents a kg on their April-June lows. Apart from the first week in January, this is the highest price recorded this year. Young domestic
cattle also sold on average for more than A$2.00 a kg.
Short supplies are driving markets in Queensland.
A combination of wet weather and the start of the grain harvest saw a number of Queensland processors this week down to three or four days production.
Queensland slaughter last week was 45,210 head.

Supplies in southern Australia were more plentiful and prices either did not rise or did not rise greatly. In Victoria cattle yardings increased by 11 percent and young cattle and cow prices moved slightly lower, although bullock prices rose slightly.
In New South Wales, yardings fell by three percent but over the past fortnight have been relatively high.
Price rises in the state were recorded for heavier steers and bullocks with most categories firm. Cattle slaughter in the state last week was 37,933 head.

USDA figures show marketings for September were less than expected at 84 percent of the level of last year while placements into feedlots were greater than expected at 104 percent. Numbers on feed are niow just three percent below 1995.
Cattle on feed in the U.S. has escalated sharply during the northern hemisphere summer, up six percent in July, 19 percent in August and four percent in September.

Most will be market ready from December through the first quarter of 1997. Extra supplies of grainfed beef from the U.S. late this year and into 1997 may lead to competitive pressurers again building.
Cow slaughter in the U.S. last week continued up on the year-ago level, at 149,400 head (up 19 percent).
The Japan market again strengthened slightly this week. Chilled grassfed fullsets sold for 380 cents a kg, up 10 cents. This is the highest export price sinmce late February.

In the latest Korean tender, awarded a week ago, Australian exporters secured 4,310 tonnes of the grassfed quarter beef on offer (77 percent of the total), 792 tonnes of grassfed fullsets (96 percent), abnd 600 tonnes of grainfed quarter beef (100 percent).
U.S. processors secured 3,832 tonnes of grainfed cuts (100 percent). Prices were slightly improved on the previous tender.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
